title: Learning Support Assistant for secondary-aged learners
hours: Full time, term time only. 8:30am to 3:30pm Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, and 8:30am to 4:30pm Thursday
salary: £20,158 a year for the term-time year, paid monthly
summary: We are looking for a warm, calm and resilient Learning Support Assistant to work with our secondary-aged learners (11 to 15), many of whom are autistic and/or anxious, in 1:1 and small-group settings.
about: Wribbenhall School is a small independent specialist school for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities, run on a trauma-informed, family-style nurture model.

You will help teachers deliver differentiated learning, build learners' independence, confidence and resilience, support emotional wellbeing with consistent, positive approaches, and work closely with colleagues, families and other professionals.
Experience of supporting children with autism and anxiety is valuable, but patience, empathy and a genuine commitment to children matter most. Full training will be provided, including Team Teach.
This is a temporary post to 16 July 2027, to support a period of changes in organisational support for Key Stage 4 development.
responsibilities: Model caring, respectful and compassionate behaviour towards learners and colleagues
Work closely with class teachers and other professionals to provide targeted support for learners with autism and anxiety
Assist teachers in planning and delivering differentiated learning activities, so every learner can access the curriculum
Support learners to develop independence, confidence and resilience
Use a range of communication strategies and resources to engage and motivate learners
Promote positive behaviour and emotional wellbeing, using consistent approaches in line with our behaviour policy
Monitor learner progress, share observations and contribute to review meetings
Foster positive relationships with learners, staff and families
Support the implementation of individual education and care plans
Help to create a calm and structured classroom environment
personSpecification: GCSE (or equivalent) in English and maths at grade 4 (C) or above
Level 2 or 3 Teaching Assistant or Learning Support qualification, or equivalent relevant experience
Experience of working with children or young people in a school, nurture or similar setting
Awareness of autism and anxiety, and the impact of anxiety on learning
Ability to adapt communication and activities to meet individual needs
Good organisational skills and the ability to work well as part of a small team
Understanding of safeguarding and child protection responsibilities (training is provided at induction)
Empathy, patience and a nurturing approach, with high expectations for all learners
Ability to remain calm under pressure
howToApply: Download the application form, job description and person specification, and our Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy below, or request an application pack from enquiries@wribbenhallschool.co.uk or 01299 405383.
Please complete the application form in full and return it to Ellis Wells by the closing date. We cannot accept CVs alone.
